rationale: D2 (#958): a class cannot inherit from itself, and in C++ the namespace qualifier is the whole information content of an inheritance edge. The base-class leaf clean (`split(/::|\s+/)`, last segment) discarded the qualifier, so `char_traits : std::char_traits<T>` published `char_traits extends char_traits` — a fabrication about a REAL inheritance — and `priority_tag : priority_tag<N-1>` published the same for a different instantiation. 49 edges over 1,722 real C++ files. The override resolver already refused exactly these bases (`if (base === startCls) continue`, with this reasoning); the edge they came from did not, so one rule lived in two places and only one of them had it. The gate is per-base, which the `Mixed` case at the end pins: a class whose clause has one self-cleans and one real base must KEEP the real one. The `Circle`/`Box`/`Poly` cases are the control against a gate that swallowed every base. Also pins D6: this class is the one that had the analyzer's last two regexes, and it now has none.

expectRelationships.note: D2d CONTROL: a distinct base keeps a real extends edge, through the qualifier.
a QUALIFIED TEMPLATED base (CPPD4): template arguments are arguments, never the inherited base, and the qualifier is resolved to its leaf.
D2e: the gate is PER-BASE. `Mixed : public lib::Shape, public priority_tag<2>` must keep the real base while the self-cleansing one is refused.

D2b: `::vendor::char_traits<char>` cleans to the LEAF `char_traits`, which is NOT this class's own name (`proxy`), so the edge is real and kept. The D2b fabrication was the case where the leaf DID equal the class's own name.

D2e, and the sharper half of the rule: the gate compares the base against the DERIVED class's own name, not against any other declared name. `Mixed` inheriting `priority_tag<2>` is REAL inheritance from a different class, so the edge is correct and kept — a gate that refused every base whose name appears elsewhere would lose this. What is refused is `priority_tag` naming `priority_tag`.
the override chain still resolves through a real base — the D2 gate must not break virtual dispatch.

forbidRelationships.note: D2a: `priority_tag<N-1>` is a different INSTANTIATION. Cleaning the template arguments leaves the class's own name, and the graph then asserted a class inherits from itself.

D2b: `vendor::char_traits : std::char_traits<T>` is real inheritance from a DIFFERENT class. The qualifier was the only thing that said so, and the leaf clean threw it away. This edge claimed a class inherits from itself.

the consequence of D2b, and the shape the M14 F5 probe originally found on fmt's `format_facet.do_put`. The override resolver's own self-collision guard is what already covered this; it is pinned here so the two halves of one rule cannot drift apart again.
